To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DSDV, AODV and DSR protocols are not suitable for MANET.
DSR is more suitable for small networks with low mobility and AODV is better suited for large networks with high mobility.
DSR is more efficient in terms of packet delivery ratio, average end-to-end delay and average jitter than DSDV and AODV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
investigating the performance of routing algorithms for adhoc network and to identify the factors affecting the performance of adhoc network.
the performance evaluation and analysis of routing protocols DSDV, AODV and DSR for ad hoc wireless networks.
the performance evaluation and comparative study of routing protocols DSR, DSDV and AODV in a simulated environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AODV performs best for MANETs with respect to the parameters that have been considered in the simulations.
DSR and ADOV perform significantly better than DSDV.
DSR is more appropriate for networks with low node speed and low mobility rate, while AODV is more appropriate for high mobility rate and high node speed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AODV performs best in most of the cases, followed by DSDV, and DSR performs worst.
AODV is the best routing protocol for MANETs in terms of performance.
AODV is the best choice for adhoc network routing protocol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of routing protocol depends on the application and the environment in which the ad hoc network is deployed.
DSR performs better than other protocols in terms of packet delivery ratio but AODV is more scalable than other protocols.
the routing protocols are not only dependent on the network characteristics but also on the application characteristics.
